turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip, with a nervous swallow, fidgeted with the hem of his coat and, in a voice barely above a whisper, requested permission to approach the door, explaining that he would endeavour to summon Miss Estella with the utmost politeness and care, should she prove amenable to being summoned at all. He cast a quick, apprehensive glance at Miss Havisham, hoping to discern some sign of approval or, failing that, at least not disapproval.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham observed Pip's hesitation with a faint, almost mournful smile, and inquired whether the summoning of Miss Estella presented a particular difficulty, or if some unseen obstacle detained him from fulfilling her simple request. It is, after all, merely a name, a whisper upon the air, is it not? She gestured languidly toward the door, a cascade of faded lace rustling with the movement.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip, twisting his fingers together, mumbled that the difficulty resided not in the name itself, but in a certain… timidity, perhaps, that prevented a proper articulation, especially in so grand and… imposing a place. He dared to suggest, with a downcast gaze and a perceptible blush creeping up his cheeks, that a more forceful prompting might, indeed, prove beneficial in eliciting a response from Miss Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham regarded Pip with a curious intensity, her eyes, shadowed and deep-set, seeming to bore into his very soul. She inquired, with a voice that seemed to catch on the dust motes dancing in the stagnant air, whether this… timidity, as he termed it, was a malady entirely his own, or one inherited, perhaps, from a lineage steeped in the shadows of disappointment? A faint, brittle laugh escaped her lips, a sound like the crumbling of old paper.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip, after a prolonged silence during which he avoided Miss Havisham’s piercing gaze, stammered that he believed his… disposition, as she phrased it, was simply a product of his own humble origins, and not attributable to any… inherited burden. He hoped, with a desperate sincerity, that such an explanation would be deemed sufficient, and that it would not be considered disrespectful to suggest that even the most distinguished of families might, on occasion, experience moments of… apprehension.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham observed that a humble origin, while perhaps… convenient, offered little true explanation for the anxieties that clung to a soul, did it not? She traced a skeletal finger along the decaying velvet of a nearby chair, her gaze unfocused, as if searching for echoes of a happier time, a time when such explanations would have seemed utterly superfluous. It is a curious thing, Pip, this… apprehension; it reveals far more than one might wish to know.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip, emboldened slightly by his last explanation, though still acutely aware of Miss Havisham’s scrutiny, offered that perhaps, in a place such as this, where the very air seemed laden with… reflection, it was natural for even the most steadfast of individuals to experience a degree of… heightened sensitivity. He added, hoping to deflect further inquiry, that it was a common human failing, he believed, to be susceptible to the influence of one's surroundings.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham allowed Pip's words to hang in the air, a faint smile playing on her lips, a smile that did not quite reach her eyes. She inquired whether this 'heightened sensitivity,' this susceptibility, as he phrased it, was a… deliberate cultivation, a carefully constructed shield against the realities of a world that so readily offers disappointment? It is, after all, a most… instructive defense.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip, feeling a blush creep up his neck, attempted to explain that the notion of a deliberate cultivation was, of course, entirely foreign to his understanding, and that any… perceived sensitivity was merely a consequence of his… earnest desire to observe and appreciate the… the surroundings, and to offer due respect. He hoped, with a palpable tremor in his voice, that such an explanation would not be judged as… evasive, and that it demonstrated a sincere lack of guile.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham regarded Pip with an almost clinical interest, her gaze lingering on the flush that stained his cheeks. She inquired if this 'earnest desire' to observe, to appreciate, to offer respect, was a performance, a practiced art, designed to… appease? It is, she mused aloud, a most… diverting study of the young.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip, twisting his hands together, insisted that the notion of a performance was most distressing to consider, and that his words were simply an attempt to… to convey the profound effect this place had upon him. He added, with a desperate hope that he was making himself understood, that he possessed no skill in such… such matters, and that any appearance of artifice was entirely unintentional.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham tilted her head, her gaze fixed upon Pip’s increasingly agitated hands, and remarked that distress, it appeared, could be a most convincing disguise. She questioned whether such a demonstrable discomfort stemmed from genuine feeling, or whether it was, perhaps, another carefully considered element in this… diverting study.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip, his voice barely a whisper, assured Miss Havisham that the suggestion of deliberate discomfort was the most unkind interpretation he could imagine. He explained that the effect she perceived was simply the consequence of being in such a… a remarkable and overwhelming place, and that any outward signs were reflections of an inner… a deep and sincere feeling of… of awe, and perhaps, a touch of… of being quite overcome.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham observed Pip's escalating distress with a peculiar amusement, and inquired whether this 'awe,' this 'overwhelm,' was not, perhaps, a rather convenient shield against a more… uncomfortable truth. It is so very easy, she murmured, to mistake a tremor of fear for a sigh of reverence, is it not?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip, swallowing hard, attempted to explain that the notion of fear was… entirely misplaced. He insisted that his feelings were purely those of reverence and a desire to understand, and that any tremor, if such a thing were even perceptible, was merely the consequence of a… a youthful awkwardness in the presence of such… such grandeur.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham regarded Pip with a languid wave of her hand, her lips curving into a faint, unsettling smile. She inquired whether this ‘youthful awkwardness,’ this professed reverence, was not, perhaps, a rather elaborate performance, designed to mask a… a deeper curiosity. It is, after all, so very diverting to observe the shadows that dance upon a young man’s face when confronted with the truth, is it not?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip, his cheeks flushed a deeper crimson, hastened to assure Miss Havisham that the suggestion of a performance was… entirely unfounded. He stammered that he possessed no skill in such matters, and that any perceived shadows upon his face were simply the unfortunate consequence of a most earnest desire to appear respectful and… and attentive, and that such an appearance, however imperfectly rendered, was the truest reflection of his feelings.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham inclined her head, her gaze lingering on Pip’s reddened cheeks with an almost clinical interest. She inquired, her voice a silken whisper that seemed to cling to the dust motes dancing in the weak light, whether this 'earnest desire' to appear respectful was not, perhaps, a rather… predictable response to a perceived threat. It is, after all, so very comforting to believe oneself agreeable, is it not?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip, his voice a barely audible tremor, insisted that the notion of a threat was, of course, entirely misconstrued; he merely wished to… to absorb the atmosphere, to appreciate the… the singular nature of the surroundings, and that any perceived response was simply the involuntary consequence of a most profound… and genuine… admiration.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham let out a breath that seemed to disturb the very stillness of the room, a sound like the rustling of ancient silks. She observed Pip’s increasingly frantic attempts at reassurance, a faint amusement flickering in her shadowed eyes, and inquired whether such a vehement denial of perceived misinterpretations was not, itself, a rather… illuminating demonstration of the very thing it sought to conceal. It is, after all, so very revealing, isn't it?

opening.text: Miss Havisham inquired who it was.

opening.text: Miss Havisham repeated his name, questioning if he was Pip.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip explained that he was Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, and had come to play.

opening.text: Miss Havisham instructed him to approach, requesting that he allow her to examine him closely.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked if he was unafraid of a woman who had never seen the sun since his birth.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham inquired what she touched there.

opening.text: Pip confirmed that he knew, ma’am.

opening.text: Miss Havisham pressed him to identify what she touched.

opening.text: Miss Havisham stated that she was tired and desired diversion, having finished with men and women, and urged him to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham confessed to having occasional strange thoughts, expressing a desire to witness some play, and repeated her encouragement to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham questioned whether he was sullen and obstinate.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip assured her that he was very sorry for her and regretted being unable to play at that moment, explaining that any complaint would lead to trouble with his sister, and that the unfamiliar and fine, yet melancholy, surroundings prevented him from doing so.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham mused that it was new to him, old to her, strange to him, familiar to her, and melancholy to both of them, and instructed him to call Estella.
